newsitem.title: USA: Portland General says merger not seen okayed.
newsitem.headline: Portland General says merger not seen okayed.

text.p: Portland General Corp said it and Enron Corp were informed by a senior member of the Oregon Public Utility Commission that its staff decided to recommend disapproval of their merger plan.
The decision was in the staff's final report, set to be released on April 11, Portland General said.

The staff member indicated the commission thought Enron's offer of $61 million in cost savings and rate reductions did not provide sufficient benefits to meet the statutory burden required for merger approval, the company said.
The staff member also indicated the commission's most recent formal proposal of $141 million in guaranteed cost savings and rate reductions would remain open until April 11.

"We continue to believe that our companies' joint proposal offers substantial benefits to Oregon and our customers," said Ken Harrison, Portland General chairman. "We are disappointed by the staff's position, and believe that the $141 million staff recommendation is not supportable."
Houston-based Enron and Portland General announced plans to merger last July via a tax-free stock swap valued at nearly $2.1 billion.
